The meaning is: <s>Puruṣa</s>, being of the nature of consciousness, always established as the presider—the inner, pure <s>sattva</s> that belongs to him, since it too always abides—whatever object colors it, for such an object the reflection of consciousness always exists; that being so, the status of knower is established. Thus there is never any suspicion of transformation [for <s>Puruṣa</s>]. ||17||

Commentary: These modifications of the mind, having the forms of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), error (<s>viparyaya</s>), and the rest—they are known always, at all times, by <s>Puruṣa</s>, the lord and master of the mind,

children.text:
nanu cittameva yadi sattvotkarṣāt prakāśakam tadā
                        svaparaprakāśarūpatvādātmānamarthaṃ ca prakāśayatīti tāvataiva
                        vyavahārasamāptiḥ| kiṃ grahītrantareṇetyāśaṅkāmapanetumāha ---
children.translated_text: But if the mind itself, through the excellence of <s>sattva</s>, is illuminating, then being of the nature of self-and-other-illumination, it illuminates both itself and the object—and with that alone, functional activity is complete. What need is there for another grasper?—to remove this doubt, he says:
It is not self-illuminating, because it is an object of perception (<s>dṛśya</s>). ||Kaivalya 18||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- taccittaṃ svābhāsaṃ svaprakāśakaṃ na bhavati puruṣavedyaṃ
                        bhavatīti yāvat| kutaḥ| dṛśyatvāt| yat kila dṛśyaṃ tat draṣṭṛvedyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ
                        yathā ghaṭādi| dṛśyaṃ ca cittaṃ tasmānna svābhāsam ||18||
children.translated_text: Commentary: That mind is not self-illuminating, not self-luminous—it is rather knowable by <s>Puruṣa</s>, this is the extent [of the meaning]. Why? Because it is an object of perception (<s>dṛśya</s>). Whatever is an object of perception is knowable by a seer—as is observed in the case of pots and such. And the mind is an object of perception. Therefore, it is not self-illuminating. ||18||

children.text:
nanu sādhyāviśiṣṭo+ayaṃ hetuḥ| dṛśyatvameva cittasyāsiddham| kiñca
                        svabuddhisaṃvedanadvāreṇa hitāhitaprāptiparihārarūpā vṛttayo dṛśyante|
                        tathāhi --- kruddho+ahaṃ bhīto+ahamatra me rāga ityevamādyā saṃvit
                        buddherasaṃvedane nopapadyata ityāśaṅkāmapanetumāha ---
children.translated_text: Objection: this reason is not different from what is to be proved. The perceptibility of the mind itself is unestablished. Moreover, through self-awareness of the intellect, activities in the form of seeking the beneficial and avoiding the harmful are observed. For instance: 'I am angry,' 'I am afraid,' 'here is my attachment'—such awareness would be untenable without self-awareness of the intellect—to remove this doubt, he says:
And at one time, there is no ascertainment of both [subject and object simultaneously]. ||Kaivalya 19||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- arthasya saṃvittiridantayā vyavahārayogyatāpādanam| ayamarthaḥ
                        sukhaheturduḥkhaheturveti| buddheḥ saṃvidahamityevamākāreṇa
                        sukhaduḥkharūpatayā vyavahārakṣamatāpādanam| evaṃvidhaṃ ca
                        vyāpāradvayamarthapratyakṣakāle na yugapat kartuṃ śakyaṃ virodhāt| na hi
                        viruddhayorvyāpārayoryugapat sambhavo+asti| ata ekasmin kāla ubhayasya
                        svarūpasyā+arthasya cāvadhārayitumaśakyatvānna cittaṃ svaprakāśakaṃ bhavati|
                        kintu evaṃvidhavyāpāradvayaniṣpādyasya
                        phaladvayasyāsaṃvedanādbahirmukhatayaiva svaniṣṭhatvena cittasya svayaṃ
                        vedanādarthaniṣṭhameva phalaṃ na svaniṣṭhamityarthaḥ ||19||
children.translated_text: Commentary: The cognition of an object is bringing it to functional awareness in the form of 'this.' The meaning is: 'this is a cause of pleasure, this is a cause of pain,' and so forth. The awareness of the intellect is bringing it to functional awareness in the form of 'I,' in the form of pleasure and pain. Such a twofold operation—at the time of perceiving an object—cannot be performed simultaneously, because of contradiction. For it is impossible for two contradictory operations to occur simultaneously. Therefore, at one time, because of the inability to ascertain both the nature of oneself and of the object, the mind is not self-illuminating. Rather, since the twofold fruit to be accomplished by such twofold operation is not cognized simultaneously—through outward direction alone, being self-established, the mind's self-cognition produces only the fruit pertaining to the object, not the fruit pertaining to itself—this is the meaning. ||19||

children.text:
nanu mā bhūdbuddheḥ svayaṃ grahaṇaṃ buddhyantareṇa bhaviṣyatītyāśaṅkyāha
                        ---
children.translated_text: Objection: let the mind not grasp itself; it will be grasped by another mind—anticipating this, he says:
If the mind were perceived by another mind, there would be an infinite regress of cognitions of cognitions, and confusion of memory. ||Kaivalya 20||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- yadi hi buddhirbuddhyantareṇa vedyate sā+api buddhiḥ svayamabuddhā
                        buddhyantaraṃ prakāśayitumasamartheti tasyā grāhakaṃ

buddhyantaraṃ kalpanīyaṃ tasyā+apyanyadityanavasthānāt
                        puruṣāntareṇārthapratītirna syāt| na hi pratītavapratītāyāmarthaḥ pratīto
                        bhavati| smṛtisaṃkaraśca prāpnoti --- rūpe rase vā samutpannāyāṃ buddhau
                        tadgrāhikāṇāmanantānāṃ buddhīnāṃ samutpatterbuddhijanitaiḥ saṃskārairyadā
                        yugapadbahvayaḥ smṛtayaḥ kriyante tadā buddheraparyavasānādbuddhismṛtīnāṃ ca
                        bahvīnāṃ yugapadutpatteḥ kasminnarthe smṛtiriyamutpanneti jñātumaśkyatvāt
                        smṛtīnāṃ saṃkaraḥ syāt| iyaṃ rūpe smṛtiriyaṃ rase smṛtiriti na jñāyeta
                        ||20||
children.translated_text: another intellect would have to be postulated for it, and for that still another—thus, due to infinite regress, no cognition of an object by a [separate] <s>Puruṣa</s> would be possible. For when cognitions are not cognized, the object is not cognized. And the confusion of memories would follow: when a cognition arises regarding form or taste, from the arising of innumerable cognitions that grasp it, when the impressions born of cognitions simultaneously produce many memories, then, because there is no end to cognitions, and because many cognitions and memories arise simultaneously, since it would be impossible to know 'this memory arose regarding which object,' there would be a confusion of memories. 'This is a memory of form, this is a memory of taste'—this would not be known. ||20||
Commentary: For if intellect is known by another intellect, that intellect too, being itself unintelligent, would be incapable of illuminating another intellect—therefore, a grasping

children.text:
nanu buddheḥ svaprakāśatvābhāve buddhyantare cāsaṃvedane kathamayaṃ
                        viṣayasaṃvedanarūpo vyavahāra ityāśaṅkya svasiddhāntamāha ---
children.translated_text: Now, if there is no self-luminosity of the intellect, and no awareness by another intellect, how does this activity in the form of object-awareness occur?—anticipating this objection, he states his own doctrine:
When <s>citi</s> (consciousness), which does not pass over, assumes the form of that [intellect], there is self-awareness of one's own intellect. ||Kaivalya 21||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- puruṣaścidrūpatvāccitiḥ sā+apratisaṃkramā| na vidyate
                        pratisakramo+anyatra gamanaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathoktā| anyenāsaṅkīrṇeti yāvat|
                        yathā guṇā aṅgāṅgibhāvalakṣaṇe pariṇāme aṅginaṃ guṇaṃ saṃkrāmanti
                        tadrūpatāmivā+a+apadyante| yathā vā loke paramāṇavaḥ prasaranto
                        viṣayamārūpayanti

naivaṃ citiśaktistasyāḥ
                        sarvadaikarūpatayā supratiṣṭhitatvena vyavasthitatvāt| atastatsannidhāne
                        yadā buddhistadākāratāmāpadyate cetanevopajāyate
children.translated_text: not so the power of <s>citi</s> (consciousness); because of being well-established in its eternally uniform nature. Therefore, in its proximity, when the intellect assumes the form of that [consciousness], the capacity for awareness arises—
and when the power of consciousness, having received the reflection of the mental activity, is perceived as being qualified by the mental activity,

children.text:
tadā buddheḥ
                        svasyā ātmano vedanaṃ saṃvedanaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ ||21||
children.translated_text: then there is the awareness, the self-awareness, of one's own intellect—this is the meaning. ||21||

Commentary: <s>Puruṣa</s>, being of the nature of consciousness, is <s>citi</s>; it does not pass over (<s>apratisaṃkramā</s>)—there is no passing over, no going to another; it is so called because it is unmixed with another. Just as the <s>guṇas</s>, in the transformation characterized by the principal-subordinate relation, pass into the principal <s>guṇa</s> and take on its form, as it were; or just as in the world, atoms extending take on the form of the object—

children.text:
itthaṃ svasaṃviditaṃ cittaṃ sarvānugrahaṇasāmarthyena
                        sakalavyavahāranirvāhakṣamaṃ bhaviṣyatītyāha ---
children.translated_text: Thus, the mind that has self-awareness, through the capacity of grasping everything, will be capable of sustaining all worldly activity—he says:
The mind, colored by the seer and the seen, is capable of [comprehending] all objects. ||Kaivalya 22||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- draṣṭā puruṣastenoparaktaṃ tatsannidhānena tadrūpatāmiva prāpnoti
                        dṛśyoparaktaṃ viṣayoparaktaṃ gṛhītaviṣayākārapariṇāmaṃ yadā bhavati tadā
                        tadeva cittaṃ sarvārthagrahaṇasamarthaṃ bhavati| yathā nirmalaṃ
                        sphaṭikadarpaṇādyeva pratibimbagrahaṇasamartham| evaṃ
                        rajastamobhyāmanabhibhūtaṃ sattvaṃ śuddhatvāccicchāyāgrahaṇasamarthaṃ
                        bhavati| na punaraśuddhatvādrajastamasī| tannyagbhūtarajastamorūpamaṅgitayā
                        sattvaṃ niścalapradīpaśikhākāraṃ sadaikarūpatayā pariṇamamānaṃ
                        cicchāyāgrahaṇasāmarthyādāmokṣaprāpteravatiṣṭhate| yathā+ayaskāntasannidhāne
                        lohasya calanamāvirbhavatyevaṃ cidrūpapuruṣasannidhāne
                        sattvasyābhivyaṅgyamabhivyajyate caitanyam| ata evāsmindarśane dve cicchaktī
                        --- nityoditā+abhivyaṅgyā ca| nityoditā cicchaktiḥ
                        puruṣasannidhānādabhivyaktamabhivyaṅgyacaitanyaṃ sattvam| abhivyaṅgyā
                        cicchaktistadatyantasannihitatvādantaraṅgaṃ puruṣasya bhogyatāṃ
                        pratipadyate| tadeva śāntabrahmavādibhiḥ sāṃkhyaiḥ puruṣasya
                        paramātmano+adhiṣṭheyaṃ karmānurūpaṃ sukhaduḥkhabhoktṛtayā vyapadiśyate|
                        yattvanudriktatvādekasyāpi guṇasya kadācit kasyacidaṅgitvāt triguṇaṃ
                        pratikṣaṇaṃ pariṇamamānaṃ sukhaduḥkhamohātmakamanirmalaṃ tattasmin
                        karmānurūpe śuddhe sattve svākārasamarpaṇadvāreṇa saṃvedyatāmāpādayati
                        tacchuddhamādyaṃ cittasattvameveti pratisaṅkrāntacicchāyamanyato
                        gṛhītaviṣayākāreṇa cittenopaḍhaukitamākāraṃ citsaṅkrāntibalāt cetanāyamānaṃ
                        vāstavacaitanyābhāve+api sukhaduḥkhasvarūpaṃ bhogamanubhavati| sa evaṃ
                        bhogo+atyantasannidhānena vivekāgrahaṇādabhokturapi puruṣasya bhoga iti
                        vyapadiṣyate| anenaivābhiprāyeṇa vindhyavāsinoktam --- sattvatapyatvameva
                        puruṣatapyatvamiti| anyatrāpi --- pratibimbe
                        pratibimbamānacchāyāsadṛśacchāyodbhavaḥ pratibimbaśabdenocyate| evaṃ
                        sattve+api pauruṣeyacicchāyāsadṛśacidabhivyaktiḥ pratisaṅkrāntiśavdārtha
                        iti| nanu pratibimbaṃ nāma nirmalasya niyatapariṇāmasya nirmale dṛṣṭam|
                        yathā mukhasya darpaṇe| atyantanirmalasya vyāpakasyāpariṇāminaḥ puruṣasya
                        tasmādatyantanirmalāt puruṣādanirmale sattve kathaṃ pratibimbanamupapadyate|
                        ucyate --- pratibimbanasya svarūpamanavagacchatā bhavatedamabhyadhāyi| yaiva
                        sattvagatāyā abhivyaṅgyāyāścicchakteḥ puruṣasya sānnidhyādabhivyaktiḥ saiva
                        pratibimbanamucyate| yādṛśī puruṣagatā cicchaktistacchāyāpyatrāvirbhavati|
                        yadapyuktamatyantanirmalaḥ puruṣaḥ kathamanirmale sattve pratisaṃkrāmatīti
                        tadapyanaikāntikam| nairmalyādapakṛṣṭe+api jalādāvādityādayaḥ
                        pratisaṃkrāntāḥ samupalabhyante| yadapyuktamanavacchinnasya nāsti
                        pratisaṃkrāntiriti tadapyayuktaṃ vyāpakasyāpyākāśasya darpanādau
                        pratisaṃkrāntidarśanāt| evaṃ sati na kācidanupapattiḥ pratibimbadarśanasya|
                        nanu sāttvikapariṇāmarūpe buddhisattve
                        puruṣasannidhānādabhivyaṅgyāyāścicchakterbāhyākārasaṃkrāntau puruṣasya
                        sukhaduḥkharūpo bhoga ityuktam tadanupapannam| tadeva cittasattvaṃ
                        prakṛtāvapariṇatāyāṃ kathaṃ sambhavati kimarthaśca tasyāḥ pariṇāmaḥ|
                        athocyeta puruṣasyārthopabhogasampādanaṃ tayā kartavyam| ataḥ
                        puruṣārthakartavyatayā+asyā yukta eva pariṇāmaḥ| taccānupapannam|
                        puruṣārthakartavyatāyā evānupapatteḥ| puruṣārtho mayā kartavya
                        evaṃvidho+adhyavasāyaḥ puruṣārthakartavyatocyate| jaḍāyāśca prakṛteḥ kathaṃ
                        prathamamevaṃvidho+adhyavasāyaḥ| asti cedadhyavasāyaḥ kathaṃ jaḍatvam|
                        atrocyate --- anulomapratilomalakṣaṇapariṇāmadvaye sahajaṃ śaktidvayamasti|
                        tadeva puruṣārthakartavyatocyate| sā ca śaktiracetanāyā api prakṛteḥ
                        sahajaiva| tatra mahadādimahābhūtaparyanto+asyā bahirmukhatayā+anulomaḥ
                        pariṇāmaḥ| punaḥ svakāraṇānupraveśanadvāreṇāsmitā+antaḥ pariṇāmaḥ
                        pratilomaḥ| itthaṃ puruṣasya bhogaparisamāpteḥ

sahajaśaktidvayakṣayāt kṛtārthā prakṛtirna
                        punaḥ pariṇāmamārabhate| evaṃvidhāyāṃ ca puruṣārthakartavyatāyāṃ jaḍāyā api
                        prakṛterna kācidanupapattiḥ| nanu yadīdṛśī śaktiḥ sahajaiva pradhānasyāsti
                        tat kimarthaṃ mokṣārthibhirmokṣāya yatnaḥ kriyate| mokṣasya cānarthanīyatve
                        tadupadeśakaśāstrasyānarthakyaṃ syāt| ucyate --- yo+ayaṃ
                        prakṛtipuruṣayoranādirbhogyabhoktṛtvalakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: due to the exhaustion of the twofold innate power, <s>Prakṛti</s>, having fulfilled its purpose, does not again begin transformation. And in such a purpose-accomplishment for <s>Puruṣa</s>, even for insentient <s>Prakṛti</s>, there is no impossibility. Now, if such a power is indeed innate to <s>Pradhāna</s>, then why do those desirous of liberation make effort for liberation? And if liberation requires no effort, the scripture that teaches it would be purposeless. It is answered: this beginningless connection between <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, characterized by the relationship of enjoyed and enjoyer—

children.text:
sambandhastasmin sati vyaktacetanāyāḥ
                        prakṛteḥ kartṛtvābhimānādduḥkhānubhave sati kathamiyaṃ
                        duḥkhanivṛttirātyantikī mama syāditi bhavatyevādhyavasāyaḥ| ato
                        duḥkhanivṛttyupāyopadeśakaśāstropadeśāpekṣā+astyeva pradhānasya|
                        tathābhūtameva karmānurūpaṃ buddhisattvaṃ śāstropadeśasya viṣayaḥ|
                        darśanāntareṣvapyevaṃvidha evāvidyāsvabhāvaḥ śāstre+adhikriyate
children.translated_text: when that exists, since <s>Prakṛti</s> with manifested consciousness, due to the ego of agency, experiences suffering, the deliberation 'how can this absolute cessation of suffering be mine?' does indeed arise. Therefore, <s>Pradhāna</s> indeed has need for the teaching of scripture that instructs in the means for the cessation of suffering. Such <s>buddhisattva</s> (intellect-purity), in accordance with <s>karma</s>, is the proper object of scriptural teaching. In other philosophical systems too, ignorance of just this nature is addressed by scripture—

children.text:
| sa ca mokṣāya prayatamāna evaṃvidhaśāstropadeśaṃ
                        sahakāriṇamapekṣya mokṣākhyaṃ phalamāsādayati| sarvāṇyeva kāryāṇi prāptāyāṃ
                        sāmagryāmātmānaṃ labhante| asya pratilomapariṇāmadvāreṇaivotpādyasya
                        mokṣākhyasya kāryasyedṛśyeva sāmagrī pramāṇena niścitā
                        prakārāntareṇānupapatteḥ| atastāṃ vinā kathaṃ bhavitumarhati| ataḥ
                        sthitametat --- saṃkrāntaviṣayoparāgamabhivyaktacicchāyaṃ buddhisattvaṃ
                        viṣayaniścayadvāreṇa samagrāṃ lokayātrāṃ nirvāhayatīti| evaṃvidhameva cittaṃ
                        paśyanto bhrāntāḥ svasaṃvedanaṃ cittaṃ cittamātraṃ ca jagadityevaṃ bruvāṇāḥ
                        pratibodhitā bhavanti ||22||
children.translated_text: and that [<s>Prakṛti</s>], striving for liberation, depending on such scriptural teaching as an auxiliary, achieves the fruit called liberation. All effects realize themselves when the complete set of conditions is present. For this effect called liberation, to be produced through the counter-evolutionary process alone, just this kind of set of conditions has been established by valid knowledge, since it is impossible otherwise. Without that, how could it exist? Therefore, it stands established: the <s>buddhisattva</s>, with the coloring of objects transferred to it and the shadow of consciousness manifested in it, sustains the entirety of worldly activity through the determination of objects. Those who, seeing the mind as being of just this nature, are deluded—saying 'the mind is self-aware,' 'the mind alone is the self,' 'the world is nothing but mind'—are [thereby] corrected. ||22||

Commentary: The seer is <s>Puruṣa</s>; colored by him, through his proximity, it attains his form, as it were. Colored by the seen, colored by objects, having undergone the transformation of assuming the form of grasped objects—when it becomes such, then that very mind becomes capable of grasping all objects. Just as a stainless crystal mirror and the like alone are capable of grasping reflections, so too <s>sattva</s>, when not overwhelmed by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, becomes capable of grasping the shadow of consciousness due to its purity; but not <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, due to their impurity. That <s>sattva</s>, with <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> subordinated to it, as the principal, transforming in a uniform manner like the flame of a steady lamp, by virtue of its capacity to grasp the shadow of consciousness, remains so until the attainment of liberation. Just as the movement of iron manifests in the proximity of a magnet, so in the proximity of <s>Puruṣa</s>, who is of the nature of consciousness, the consciousness that is to be manifested in <s>sattva</s> is manifested. Therefore, in this philosophical system, there are two powers of consciousness: the eternally arisen and the to-be-manifested. The eternally arisen power of consciousness belongs to <s>Puruṣa</s>; <s>sattva</s> is the manifested, to-be-manifested consciousness. The to-be-manifested power of consciousness, because of being in extreme proximity to <s>Puruṣa</s>, internally becomes the object of experience for <s>Puruṣa</s>. That very same is designated by the peaceful <s>Brahmavādins</s> and <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> as the superintended of <s>Puruṣa</s>, the supreme Self, experiencing happiness and suffering in accordance with <s>karma</s>. But since at any time, due to predominance, one of the <s>guṇas</s> becomes principal, the three-<s>guṇa</s> [composite], transforming every moment, whose nature is happiness, suffering, and delusion, impure—in that pure <s>sattva</s>, in accordance with <s>karma</s>, through the offering of its own form, it creates awareness. That pure, primary <s>cittasattva</s>, having received the reflection of consciousness, with the form offered to it by the mind which has grasped objects from elsewhere, becoming sentient by the force of the transmission of consciousness—even in the absence of actual consciousness—experiences enjoyment in the form of happiness and suffering. That enjoyment, due to extreme proximity, due to non-apprehension of discrimination, is designated as the enjoyment of <s>Puruṣa</s>, even though <s>Puruṣa</s> is not an experiencer. With this very intention, <s>Vindhyavāsin</s> stated: 'The being-heated of <s>sattva</s> is itself the being-heated of <s>Puruṣa</s>.' Elsewhere too: 'In a reflection, the appearance of a shadow similar to the shadow of what is reflected is called by the word 'reflection.' Likewise, in <s>sattva</s> too, the manifestation of consciousness similar to the shadow of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s consciousness is the meaning of the word 'reflection.'' Now, reflection is observed of what is stainless, undergoing definite transformation, in something stainless—as of the face in a mirror. Of <s>Puruṣa</s>, who is extremely stainless, pervading, and non-transforming—how can there be a reflection from that extremely stainless <s>Puruṣa</s> in the impure <s>sattva</s>? It is answered: this was asserted by one who does not understand the true nature of reflection. The very manifestation, due to the proximity of <s>Puruṣa</s>, of the to-be-manifested power of consciousness residing in <s>sattva</s>—that itself is called reflection. Whatever the power of consciousness residing in <s>Puruṣa</s> is like, its shadow also manifests here. As for the objection 'how does the extremely stainless <s>Puruṣa</s> reflect in the impure <s>sattva</s>?'—that too is not conclusive, for even in water and the like, which are far from stainless, the sun and such are observed as reflected. As for the objection 'the undelimited has no reflection'—that too is incorrect, for even of space, which is all-pervading, reflection is observed in a mirror and the like. This being so, there is no impossibility for the observation of reflection. Now, it was said that in the <s>sattva</s> of the intellect, which is a <s>sāttvika</s> transformation, due to the proximity of <s>Puruṣa</s>, when the external form is transmitted along with the to-be-manifested power of consciousness, <s>Puruṣa</s>'s enjoyment is in the form of happiness and suffering—that is untenable, [one might say]. How does that very <s>cittasattva</s> arise when <s>Prakṛti</s> has not transformed, and for what purpose is her transformation? If it be said that she must accomplish the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s object-enjoyment, and therefore transformation is appropriate for her because of the necessity of accomplishing <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose—that too is untenable, because the very necessity of accomplishing <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose is untenable. 'The purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> must be accomplished by me'—such determination is what is called 'the necessity of accomplishing <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose.' But how can insentient <s>Prakṛti</s> initially have such determination? If there is determination, how can there be insentience? Here it is answered: in the twofold transformation characterized as evolutionary and counter-evolutionary, there exists an innate twofold power. That itself is called 'the necessity of accomplishing <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose.' And that power, even of insentient <s>Prakṛti</s>, is indeed innate. Therein, the evolutionary transformation of <s>Prakṛti</s>, proceeding outward from <s>mahat</s> to the great elements, constitutes her forward transformation. The counter-evolutionary transformation, through re-entry into her own causes up to <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness), constitutes her reverse transformation. Thus, until the completion of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s enjoyment,

children.text:
nanu yadyevaṃvidhādeva cittāt sakalavyavahāraniṣpattiḥ kathaṃ pramāṇaśūnyo
                        draṣṭā+abhyupagamyata ityāśaṅkya draṣṭuḥ pramāṇamāha ---
children.translated_text: Now, if all worldly activity is accomplished from just such a mind, how is the seer, devoid of any means of valid knowledge, accepted?—anticipating this objection, he states the proof of the seer:
That [mind], though variegated by innumerable <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions), exists for another's purpose, because it acts in association. ||Kaivalya 23||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- tadeva cittaṃ saṃkhyātumaśakyābhirvāsanābhiścitramapi nānārūpamapi
                        parārthaṃ parasya svāmino bhokturbhogāpavargalakṣaṇamarthaṃ sādhayatīti|
                        kutaḥ| saṃhatyakāritvāt saṃhatya sambhūya militvā+arthakriyākāritvāt| yacca
                        saṃhatyārthakriyākāri tat parārthaṃ dṛṣṭam| yathā śayanāsanādi|
                        sattvarajastamāṃsi ca cittalakṣaṇapariṇāmabhāñji saṃhatyakārīṇi caātaḥ
                        parārthāni| yaḥ paraḥ sa puruṣaḥ| nanu yādṛśena śayanāsanādīnāṃ pareṇa
                        śarīravatā pārārthyamupalabdhaṃ taddṛṣṭāntabalena tādṛśa eva paraḥ sidhyati|
                        yādṛśaśca bhavatāṃ paro+asaṃhatarūpo+abhipretastadviparītasya
                        siddherayamiṣṭavighātakṛddhetuḥ| ucyate --- yadyapi sāmānyena parārthamātre
                        vyāptirgṛhītā tathā+api sattvādivilakṣaṇadharmiparyālocanayā tadvilakṣaṇa
                        eva bhoktā paraḥ sidhyati| yathā candanāvṛte śikhariṇi
                        vilakṣaṇāddhūmādvahniranumīyamāna itaravahnivilakṣaṇaścandanaprabhava eva
                        pratīyate| evamihāpi vilakṣaṇasya sattvākhyasya bhogyasya
                        parārthatve+anumīyamāne tathāvidha eva bhoktā+adhiṣṭhātā
                        paraścinmātrarūpo+asaṃhataḥ sidhyati| yadi ca tasya paratvaṃ
                        sarvotkṛṣṭatvamevaṃ pratīyate tathāpi tāmasebhyo viṣayebhyaḥ prakṛṣyate
                        śarīraṃ prakāśarūpendriyāśrayatvāt| tasmādapi prakṛṣyante indriyāṇi|
                        tato+api prakṛṣṭaṃ sattvaṃ prakāśarūpam| tasyāpi yaḥ prakāśakaḥ
                        prakāśyavilakṣaṇaḥ sa cidrūpa eva

children.translated_text: is established — so how could there be compositeness in him? || 23 ||

Commentary: That very mind, though variegated with innumerable <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions), though manifold in form, serves another's purpose — it accomplishes the aim characterized by enjoyment and liberation for the other, the master, the experiencer. Why? Because it acts in conjunction (<s>saṃhatyakāritva</s>). Because it functions by combining, coming together, joining to accomplish its purpose. And whatever acts in conjunction for the accomplishment of a purpose is seen to serve another — like a bed, seat, and so forth. <s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, which undergo transformations of the nature of mind, act in conjunction and are therefore for another's purpose. He who is that other is <s>Puruṣa</s>. Now, the kind of other for whom the serving of another purpose has been observed in beds, seats, and the like — namely, an embodied being — by the force of that example, only such an other would be established. And the kind of other that you intend — one of non-composite nature — the establishment of the opposite would be a fault undermining your desired conclusion. The reply is: although the invariable connection has been grasped with merely 'for another's purpose' in general, still, through the consideration of the substance possessing properties distinct from <s>sattva</s> and the rest, the experiencer who is distinct from them is established as the other. Just as, on a mountain covered with sandalwood, fire inferred from smoke distinct [from ordinary smoke] is understood as different from ordinary fire — as having its origin in sandalwood — so here too, when the serving of another purpose is being inferred for the thing called <s>sattva</s>, which is the object of enjoyment, distinct [from ordinary objects], the experiencer, the presider, who is the other, of the nature of pure consciousness alone, non-composite,

children.text: idānīṃ śāstraphalaṃ kaivalyaṃ nirṇetuṃ daśabhiḥ sūtrairupakramate ---
children.translated_text: Now, to determine <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation), the fruit of the teaching, he begins with ten <s>sūtras</s>—
For one who sees the distinction [between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>], the contemplation of the nature of the self ceases. || Kaivalya 24 ||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- evaṃ sattvapuruṣayoranyatve sādhite yastayorviśeṣaṃ paśyati ---
                        ayamasmādanya ityevaṃrūpam --- tasya vijñātacittarūpasattvasya citte
                        yā+a+atmabhāvabhāvanā sā nivartate| cittameva kartṛ jñātṛ bhoktrityabhimāno
                        nivartate ||24||
children.translated_text: Commentary: When the otherness of <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> has been thus established, for one who sees their distinction — of the form 'this is other than that' — for him, the contemplation of selfhood in the mind, whose nature as <s>sattva</s> has been understood, ceases. The false identification that 'the mind alone is the agent, knower, experiencer' ceases. || 24 ||
When that has occurred, what happens? He says—
Then the mind inclines toward discrimination and gravitates toward <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). || Kaivalya 25 ||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- yadasyājñānanimnapathaṃ bahirmukhaṃ viṣayopabhogaphalaṃ
                        cittamāsīttadidānīṃ vivekanimnaṃ vivekamārgamantarmukhaṃ kaivalyaprāgbhāraṃ
                        kaivalyaprārambhaṃ sampadyata iti ||25||
children.translated_text: Commentary: That mind of his which previously followed the path sloping toward ignorance, facing outward, bearing the fruit of enjoyment of objects — that now inclines toward discrimination, follows the path of discrimination, facing inward, gravitating toward <s>kaivalya</s>, beginning its approach to liberation. || 25 ||

children.text:
asmiṃśca vivekavāhini citte ye+antarāyāḥ prādurbhavantiteṣāṃ
                        hetupratipādanadvāreṇa tyāgopāyamāha ---
children.translated_text: And in this mind flowing with discrimination, he states the method of abandoning the obstacles that arise, through teaching their cause—
In the gaps of that [discrimination], other cognitions arise from <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions). || Kaivalya 26 ||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- tasmin samādhau sthitasya chidreṣvantarāyeṣu yāni pratyayāntarāṇi
                        vyutthānarūpāṇi jñānāni prāgbhūtebhyaḥ vyutthānānubhavajebhyaḥ
                        saṃskārebhyo+ahaṃ mametyevaṃrūpāṇi kṣīyamāṇebhyo+api prādurbhavanti|
                        antaḥkaraṇocchittidvāreṇa teṣāṃ hānaṃ kartavyamityuktaṃ bhavati ||26||
children.translated_text: Commentary: For one established in that <s>samādhi</s>, in the gaps — the interruptions — other cognitions of the nature of emergence, in the form of 'I' and 'mine,' arise from previously existing <s>saṃskāras</s> born of the experience of emergence, even though those impressions are diminishing. Their removal should be accomplished through the cutting off of the inner instrument — this is what is stated. || 26 ||
The method of removal has already been stated, he says—
The removal of these is said to be like [the removal of] the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). || Kaivalya 27 ||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- yathā kleśānāmavidyādīnāṃ hānaṃ pūrvamuktam (2|10--11) tathā
                        saṃskārāṇāmapi kartavyam| yathā te jñānāgninā pluṣṭā dagdhabījakalpā na
                        punaścittabhūmau prarohaṃ labhante tathā saṃskārā api ||27||
children.translated_text: Commentary: Just as the removal of the <s>kleśas</s> — <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the rest — was previously stated (2.10-11), so too should it be done for these <s>saṃskāras</s>. Just as those [<s>kleśas</s>], scorched by the fire of knowledge, become like burnt seeds and do not sprout again in the field of the mind, so too the <s>saṃskāras</s>. || 27 ||

children.text:
evaṃ ca pratyayāntarāntarānudaye sthirībhūte samādhau yādṛśasya yoginaḥ
                        samādheḥ prakarṣaprāptirbhavati tathāvidhamupāyamāha ---
children.translated_text: Thus, when the arising of intervening cognitions has ceased and <s>samādhi</s> has become stable, he states the means by which the yogin's <s>samādhi</s> reaches its highest excellence—

For one who has no interest even in the highest meditation (<s>prasaṅkhyāna</s>), from <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative knowledge) in every way, there arises the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>dharmamegha</s> (cloud of dharma). || Kaivalya 28 ||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- prasaṃkhyānaṃ yāvatāṃ tattvānāṃ yathākramaṃ vyavasthitānāṃ
                        parasparavilakṣaṇasvarūpavibhāvanam| tasmin satyapyakusīdasya phalamalipsoḥ
                        pratyayāntarāṇāmanudaye sarvaprakāravivekakhyāteḥ pariśeṣāddharmameghaḥ
                        samādhirbhavati| prakṛṣṭamaśuklakṛṣṇaṃ dharmaṃ paramapuruṣārthasādhakaṃ
                        mehati siñcatīti dharmameghaḥ| anena prakṛṣṭadharmasyaiva
                        jñānahetutvamityupapāditaṃ bhavati ||28||
children.translated_text: Commentary: <s>Prasaṅkhyāna</s> (highest meditation) is the discernment of the distinctive natures of all the principles arranged in their proper order, each being different from the others. Even when that exists, for one who has no self-interest, who does not desire fruit, when intervening cognitions no longer arise, from <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative knowledge) in every way, by elimination, the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>dharmamegha</s> (cloud of <s>dharma</s>) arises. It is so called because it rains (<s>mehati</s>), pours forth, the supreme <s>dharma</s> — the exalted, neither-white-nor-black <s>dharma</s> that accomplishes the highest purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>. By this it is demonstrated that exalted <s>dharma</s> alone is the cause of knowledge. || 28 ||
From that <s>dharmamegha</s>, what happens? He says—
From that comes the cessation of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>karma</s> (actions). || Kaivalya 29 ||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- kleśānāmavidyādīnāmabhiniveśāntānāṃ karmaṇāṃ ca śuklādibhedena
                        trividhānāṃ jñānodayāt pūrvapūrvakāraṇanivṛtyā nivṛttirbhavati ||29||
children.translated_text: Commentary: The cessation of the <s>kleśas</s> — from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) up to <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life) — and of the three kinds of <s>karma</s>, distinguished as white and the rest, occurs through the arising of knowledge, by the successive removal of each preceding cause. || 29 ||
When these have ceased, what happens? He says—
Then, because of the infinity of knowledge freed from all coverings and impurities, what remains to be known is little. || Kaivalya 30 ||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- āvriyate cittamebhirityāvaraṇāni kleśāsta eva malāstebhyo+apetasya
                        tadvirahitasya jñānasya gagananibhasyānantyādanavacchedājjñeyamalpaṃ
                        gaṇanāspadaṃ bhavati| akleśenaiva sarvaṃ jñeyaṃ jānātītyarthaḥ ||30||
children.translated_text: Commentary: The coverings are the <s>kleśas</s>, by which the mind is covered; they themselves are the impurities. For knowledge freed from these — devoid of them — resembling the sky, because of its infinity, its boundlessness, what remains to be known becomes trivial, hardly worth counting. Without effort, one knows all that is to be known — this is the meaning. || 30 ||
From that, what happens? He says—
From that comes the end of the sequence of transformations of the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents), whose purpose has been fulfilled. || Kaivalya 31 ||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- kṛto niṣpādito bhogāpavargalakṣaṇaḥ puruṣārthaḥ prayojanaṃ yaiste
                        kṛtārthāḥ| guṇāḥ sattvarajastamāṃsi| teṣāṃ pariṇāma
                        āpuruṣārthasamāpterānulomyena prātilomyenāṅgāṅgibhāvaḥ sthitilakṣaṇaḥ| tasya
                        yo+asau kramo vakṣyamāṇastasya parisamāptirniṣṭhā| na punarudbhava ityarthaḥ
                        ||31||
children.translated_text: Commentary: Those whose purpose has been fulfilled — for whom the <s>puruṣārtha</s> (purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>), characterized by enjoyment and liberation, has been accomplished — are called <s>kṛtārtha</s> (those whose purpose is fulfilled). The <s>guṇas</s> are <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. Their transformation — the mutual relation of principal and subsidiary, characterized by stability, proceeding favorably and unfavorably until the completion of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose — of that, the sequence about to be described, its complete end, its conclusion. There is no further arising — this is the meaning. || 31 ||
He states the definition of the sequence that was mentioned—
Sequence is the counterpart of a moment, graspable at the terminal point of a transformation. || Kaivalya 32 ||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- kṣaṇo+alpīyān kālastasya yo+asau pratiyogī kṣaṇavilakṣaṇaḥ
                        pariṇāmāparāntanirgrāhyo+anubhūteṣu kṣaṇeṣu paścāt saṃkalanabuddhyaiva yo
                        gṛhyate sa kṣaṇānāṃ krama ucyate| na hyananubhūteṣu kramaḥ parijñātuṃ śakyaḥ
                        ||32||
children.translated_text: Commentary: A moment is the smallest unit of time; its counterpart — what is distinct from a single moment — is sequence, graspable at the terminal point of a transformation, grasped only afterward, through the cognition of compilation, after moments have been experienced. That is called the sequence of moments. For sequence cannot be ascertained in moments that have not been experienced. || 32 ||
Now he states the unique nature of <s>kaivalya</s>, which is the fruit—

children.text:
puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ guṇānāṃ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṃ svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā
                        citiśakteriti ||kaivalya 33||
children.translated_text: The <s>pratiprasava</s> (involution) of the <s>guṇas</s>, devoid of the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, is <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation); or it is the establishment of the power of consciousness in its own nature. || Kaivalya 33 ||

children.text:
vṛttiḥ --- samāptabhogāpavargalakṣaṇapuruṣārthānāṃ guṇānāṃ yaḥ pratiprasavaḥ
                        pratilomasya pariṇāmasya samāptau vikārānudbhavo yadi va
                        citiśaktervṛttisārūpyanivṛttau svarūpamātre+avasthānaṃ tat kaivalyamucyate
                        ||33||
children.translated_text: Commentary: Of the <s>guṇas</s> whose purpose — characterized by enjoyment and liberation — has been completed, the <s>pratiprasava</s> (involution) — the non-arising of modifications at the completion of the reverse transformation — or alternatively, when the conformity of the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>) with mental modifications has ceased, the abiding in its own essential nature alone — that is called <s>kaivalya</s>. || 33 ||

children.text:
tadevaṃ siddhyantarebhyo vilakṣaṇāṃ
                            sarvasiddhimūlabhūtāṃ samādhisiddhimabhidhāya
                            jātyantarapariṇāmalakṣaṇasya ca siddhiviśeṣasya prakṛtyāpūraṇameva
                            kāraṇamityupapādya dharmādīnāṃ pratibandhakanivṛttamātre eva
                            sāmarthyamiti pradarśya nirmāṇacittānāmasmitāmātrādudbhava ityuktvā
                            teṣāṃ ca yogicittamevādhiṣṭhāpakamiti pradarśya yogicittasya
                            cittāntaravailakṣaṇyamabhidhāya tatkarmaṇāmalaukikatvaṃ copapādya
                            vipākānuguṇānāṃ vāsanānāmabhivyaktisāmarthyaṃ
                            kāryakāraṇayoścaikyapratipādanena vyavahitānāmapi
                            vāsanānāmānantaryamupapādya tāsāmānantye+api hetuphalādidvāreṇa
                            hānamupadarśya atītādiṣvadhvasu dharmāṇāṃ sadbhāvamupapādya vijñānavādaṃ
                            nirākṛtya sākāravādaṃ ca pratiṣṭhāpya puruṣasya jñātṛtvamuktvā
                            cittadvāreṇa sakalavyavahāraniṣpattimupapādya puruṣasattve
                            pramāṇamupadarśya kaivalyanirṇayāya daśabhiḥ sūtraiḥ
                            krameṇopayogino+arthānabhidhāya śāstrāntare+apyetadeva
                            kaivalyamityupapādya kaivalyasvarūpaṃ nirṇītamiti vyākṛtaḥ
                            kaivalyapādaḥ|
children.translated_text: Thus, having described <s>samādhi</s>-accomplishment, which is the root of all accomplishments, as distinct from other <s>siddhis</s>; and having demonstrated that the filling up of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) alone is the cause of the particular <s>siddhi</s> characterized by transformation into another species; and having shown that <s>dharmas</s> and the rest have their efficacy merely upon the removal of their obstructions; and having stated that created minds arise from mere <s>asmitā</s> (ego-sense), and that the <s>yogin</s>'s mind alone is their governing authority; and having described the distinction of the <s>yogin</s>'s mind from other minds, and having demonstrated the supramundane nature of its <s>karma</s>; and having shown the power of manifestation of <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) in accordance with fruition, and having demonstrated the continuity even of obstructed <s>vāsanās</s> through establishing the unity of cause and effect; and having shown their removal through the means of cause, fruit, and so forth even when they are infinite; and having demonstrated the real existence of <s>dharmas</s> in past and other time-periods; and having refuted the <s>vijñānavāda</s> (consciousness-only doctrine) and having established the <s>sākāravāda</s> (doctrine of cognition with form); and having stated the knower-nature of <s>Puruṣa</s>, and having demonstrated the accomplishment of all worldly activity through the medium of the mind; and having shown the proof for the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s>; and having stated topics useful in sequence through ten <s>sūtras</s> for the determination of <s>kaivalya</s>; and having demonstrated that this very <s>kaivalya</s> is established in other scriptures as well — the nature of <s>kaivalya</s> has been determined. Thus has the <s>Kaivalyapāda</s> been explained.
