children.text:
iha śrībhojadevasya
                                rājamārtaṇḍavṛttirvastutaḥ samāptā| tathā+api katipayāni pṛṣṭhāni
                                pralāpapūrṇāni saṃyojitānyasmin sthāne kenacit pāṣaṇḍenā+ayauktikāni
                                tiraskṛtāni ca sarvairapi yogibhiḥ| na kevalaṃ sarvānyapi darśanāni
                                khaṇḍitāni kiñcidvedaviruddhaṃ matamapi tena pracāritam| jijñāsoḥ
                                pāṭhakasya kautūhalanivṛttyarthametāni pṛṣṭhānyatra
                                samāviṣṭāni|
children.translated_text: Here the <s>Rājamārtaṇḍa</s> commentary of the illustrious <s>Bhojadeva</s> is in substance complete. Nevertheless, a few pages full of incoherent material have been appended at this point by someone of heretical persuasion — [pages] that are illogical and rejected by all <s>yogins</s>. Not only are all philosophical systems refuted [therein], but some doctrine contrary to the <s>Vedas</s> has also been propagated by him. For the satisfaction of the curiosity of the inquiring reader, these pages have been included here.

children.text:
na kevalamasmaddarśane kṣetrajñaḥ
                            kaivalyāvasthāyāmevaṃvidhaścidrūpaḥ yāvaddarśanāntareṣvapi vimṛṣyamāṇa
                            evaṃrūpo+avatiṣṭhate| tathāhi --- saṃsāradaśāyāmātmā
                            kartṛtvabhoktṛtvānusandhātṛtvamayaḥ pratīyate+anyathā yadyayamekaḥ
                            kṣetrajñastathāvidho na syāttadā jñānakṣaṇānāmeva
                            pūrvāparānusandhātṛśūnyānāmātmabhāve niyataḥ karmaphalasambandho na syāt
                            kṛtahānākṛtābhyāgamaprasaṅgaśca| yadi yenaiva śāstropadiṣṭamanuṣṭhitaṃ
                            karma tasyaiva bhoktṛtvaṃ bhavettadā hitāhitaprāptiparihārāya sarvasya
                            pravṛttirghaṭeta sarvasyaiva vyavahārasya
                            hānopādānalakṣaṇasyānusandhānenaiva prāptatvājjñānakṣaṇānāṃ
                            parasparabhedenānusandhānaśūnyatvāt tadanusandhānābhāve kasyacidapi
                            vyavahārānupapatteḥ kartā bhoktā+anusandhātā yaḥ sa ātmeti
                            vyavasthāpyate| mokṣadaśāyāṃ tu
                            sakalagrāhyagrāhakalakṣaṇavyavahārābhāvāccaitanyamātrameva
                            tasyāvaśiṣyate taccaitanyaṃ citimātratvenaivopapadyate na
                            punarātmasaṃvedanena| yasmādviṣayagrahaṇasamarthanameva cite rūpaṃ
                            nātmagrāhakatvam| tathāhi --- arthaścityā gṛhyamāṇo+ayamiti gṛhyate
                            svarūpaṃ gṛhyamāṇamahamiti na
                            punaryugapadbahirmukhatā+antarmukhatālakṣaṇavyāpāradvayaṃ
                            parasparaviruddhaṃ kartuṃ śakyam| ata ekasmin samaye vyāpāradvayasya
                            kartumaśakyatvāccidrūpatayaivāvaśiṣyate| ato mokṣāvasthāyāṃ
                            nivṛttādhikāreṣu guṇeṣu cinmātrarūpa evātmā+avatiṣṭhat ityeva yuktam|
                            saṃsāradaśāyāṃ tu evambhūtasyaiva kartṛtvaṃ bhoktṛtvamanusandhātṛtvaṃ ca
                            sarvamupapadyate| tathāhi --- yo+ayaṃ prakṛtyā sahānādirnaisargiko+asya
                            bhogyabhoktṛtvalakṣaṇasambandho+avivekakhyātimūlaḥ| asmin sati
                            puruṣārthakartavyatārūpaśaktidvayasadbhāve yā mahadādibhāvena
                            pariṇatistasyāṃ saṃyoge sati yadātmano+adhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ
                            cicchāyāsamarpaṇasāmarthyaṃ buddhisattvasya ca
                            saṃkrāntacicchāyāgrahaṇasāmarthyaṃ cidavaṣṭabdhāyāśca buddheryo+ayaṃ
                            kartṛtvabhoktṛtvādhyavasāyastata eva sarvasyānusandhānapūrvakasya
                            vyavahārasya niṣpatteḥ kimanyaiḥ phalgubhiḥ kalpanājalpaiḥ| yadi
                            punarevambhūtamārgavyatirekeṇa pāramārthikamātmanaḥ
                            kartṛtvādyaṅgīkriyeta tadā+asya pariṇāmitvaprasaṅgaḥ|
                            pariṇāmitvāccānityatve tasyā+a+atmatvameva na syāt| yathā hyekasminneva
                            samaye ekenaikarūpeṇa na parasparaviruddhāvasthānubhavaḥ sambhavati|
                            tathāhi --- yasyāmavasthāyāmātmasamavete sukhe samutpanne
                            tasyānubhavitṛtvaṃ na tasyāmevāvasthāyāṃ duḥkhānubhavitṛtvam|
                            ato+avasthānānātvāt tadabhinnasyāvasthāvato nānātvam| nānātvācca
                            pariṇāmitvānnātmatvam| nāpi nityatvam| ata eva śāntabrahmavādibhiḥ
                            sāṃkhyairātmanaḥ sadaiva saṃsāradaśāyāṃ mokṣadaśāyāṃ caikaṃ
                            rūpamaṅgīkriyate| ye tu vedāntavādinaścidānandamayatvamātmano mokṣaṃ
                            manyante teṣāṃ na yuktaḥ pakṣaḥ| tathāhi --- ānandasya sukhasvarūpatvāt
                            sukhasya ca sadaiva saṃvedyamānatayaiva pratibhāsāt saṃvedyamānatvaṃ ca
                            saṃvedanavyatirekeṇānupapannamiti
                            saṃbedyasaṃvedanayordvayorabhyupagamādadvaitahāniḥ| atha
                            sukhātmakatvameva tasyocyeta tadviruddhadharmādhyāsādanupapannam| na hi
                            saṃvedanaṃ saṃvedyaṃ caikaṃ bhavitumarhatīti| kiñcādvaitavādibhiḥ
                            karmātmaparamātmabhedenātmā dvividhaḥ svīkṛtaḥ| itthaṃ ca tatra yenaiva
                            rūpeṇa sukhaduḥkhabhoktṛtvaṃ karmātmanastenaiva rūpeṇa yadi paramātmanaḥ
                            syāttadā karmātmavat paramātmanaḥ pariṇāmitvamavidyāsvabhāvatvaṃ ca
                            syāt| atha na tasya sākṣādbhoktṛtvaṃ kintu
                            tadupaḍhaukitamudāsīnatayā+adhiṣṭhātṛtvena svīkaroti
                            tadā+asmaddarśanānupraveśaḥ| ānandarūpatā ca pūrvameva nirākṛtā|
                            kiñcāvidyāsvabhāvatve niḥsvabhāvatvāt karmātmanāṃ kaḥ śāstrādhikārī| na
                            tāvannityanirmuktatvāt paramātmā| nāpyavidyā svabhāvatvāt karmātmā|
                            tataśca sakalaśāstravaiyarthyaprasaṅgaḥ| avidyāmayatve ca
                            jagato+aṅgīkriyamāṇe kasyāvidyeti vicāryate| na tāvat paramātmano
                            nityamuktatvādvidyārūpatvācca| karmātmano+api paramārthato
                            niḥsvabhāvatayā śaśaviṣāṇaprakhyatve kathamavidyāsambandhaḥ| athocyate
                            nama| etadevāvidyāyā avidyātvaṃ yadavicāraṇīyatvam| yaiva hi vicāreṇa
                            dinakaraspṛṣṭanīhāravadvimalamupayāti sā+avidyetyucyate| maivam|
                            yadvastu kiñcit kāryaṃ karoti tadavaśyaṃ kutaścidbhinnamabhinnaṃ vā
                            vaktavyam| avidyāyāśca saṃsāralakṣaṇakāryakartṛtvamavaśyamaṅgīkartavyam|
                            tasmin satyapi yadyanirvācyatvamucyate tadā kasyacidapi vācyatvaṃ na
                            syāt brahmaṇo+apyavācyatvaprasaktiḥ| tasmādadhiṣṭhātṛtārūpavyatirekeṇa
                            nānyadātmano rūpamupapadyate| adhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ ca cidrūpatvameva
                            tadvyatiriktasya dharmasya kasyacit pramāṇānupapatteḥ| yairapi
                            naiyāyikādibhirātmā cetanāyogāccetana ityucyate cetanāpi tasya
                            manaḥsaṃyogajā| tathāhi --- icchājñānaprayatnādayo ye guṇāstasya
                            vyavahāradaśāyāmātmamanaḥsaṃyogādutpadyante taireva ca guṇaiḥ svayaṃ
                            jñātā kartā bhokteti vyapadiśyate| mokṣadaśāyāṃ tu mithyājñānanivṛttau
                            tanmūlānāṃ doṣāṇāmapi nivṛttiḥ| teṣāṃ buddhyādīnāṃ
                            viśeṣaguṇānāmatyantocchittiḥ svarūpamātrapratiṣṭhatvamātmano+aṅgīkṛtaṃ
                            teṣāmayuktaḥ pakṣaḥ| yatastasyāṃ daśāyāṃ nityatvavyāpakatvādayo guṇā
                            ākāśādīnāmapi santi|
                            atastadvailakṣaṇyenātmanaścidrūpatvamavaśyamaṅgīkāryam|
                            ātmatvavilakṣaṇajātiyoga iti cenna| sarvasyaiva tajjātiyogaḥ sambhavati|
                            ato jātibhyo vailakṣaṇyamātmano+avaśyamaṅgīkartavyam| tasyādhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ
                            cidrūpatayaiva ghaṭate nānyathā| yairapi mīmāṃsakaiḥ karmakartṛrūpa
                            ātmā+aṅgīkriyate teṣāmapi na yuktaḥ pakṣaḥ| tathāhi ---
                            ahaṃpratyayagrāhya ātmeti teṣāṃ pratijñā| ahaṃpratyaye ca kartṛtvaṃ
                            karmatvaṃ cātmana eva| na caitadviruddhatvādupapadyate| kartṛtvaṃ
                            pramātṛtvaṃ karmatvaṃ ca prameyatvam| na caitadviruddhadharmādhyāso
                            yugapadekasya ghaṭate| yadviruddhadharmādhyastaṃ na tadekaṃ yathā
                            bhāvābhāvau| viruddhe ca kartṛtvakarmatve| athocyate --- na
                            kartṛtvakarmatvayorvirodhaḥ kintu kartṛtvakaraṇatvayoḥ| naitadyuktam|
                            viruddhadharmādhyāsasya tulyatvāt kartṛtvakarmatvayoreva virodho na
                            kartṛtvakarmatvayoḥ|
                            tasmādahaṃpratyayagrāhyatvaṃparihṛtyātmano+adhiṣṭhātṛtvamevopapannam|
                            tacca cetanatvameva| yairapi dravyabodhaparyāyabhedenātmano+avyāpakasya
                            śarīraparimāṇasya pariṇāmitvamiṣyate teṣāmutthānaparāhata eva pakṣaḥ|
                            pariṇāmitve cidrūpatāhāniḥ| cidrūpatā+abhāve kimātmana ātmatvam|
                            tasmādātmana ātmatvamicchatā cidrūpatvamevāṅgīkartavyam|
                            taccādhiṣṭhātṛtvameva| kecit kartṛrūpamevātmānamicchanti| tathāhi ---
                            viṣayasānnidhye yā jñānalakṣaṇā kriyā samutpannā tasyā viṣayasaṃvittiḥ
                            phalam| tasyāṃ ca phalarūpāyāṃ saṃvittau svarūpaṃ prakāśarūpatayā
                            pratibhāsate| viṣayaśca grāhyatayā| ātmā ca grāhakatayā| ghaṭamahaṃ
                            jānāmītyākāreṇa tasyāḥ samutpatteḥ| kriyāyāśca kāraṇaṃ karteva
                            bhavatītyataḥ kartṛtvaṃ bhoktṛtvaṃ cātmano rūpamiti| tadanupapannam|
                            yasmāttāsāṃ saṃvittīnāṃ sa kiṃ kartṛtvaṃ yugapat pratipadyate krameṇa
                            vā| yugapat kartṛtve kṣaṇāntare tasya kartṛtvaṃ na syāt| atha krameṇa
                            kartṛtvaṃ tadaikarūpasya na ghaṭate| ekena rūpeṇa cettasya katṛtvaṃ
                            tadaikasya sadaiva sannihitatvāt sarvaṃ phalamekarūpaṃ syāt| atha
                            nānārūpatayā tasya kartṛtvam| tadā pariṇāmitvam| pariṇāmitvācca na
                            cidrūpatvam| ataścidrūpatvamātmana icchadbhirna
                            sākṣātkartṛtvamaṅgīkartavyam| yādṛśamasmābhiḥ kartṛtvamātmanaḥ
                            pratipāditaṃ kūṭasthasya nityasya cidrūpasya tadevopapannam| etena
                            svaprakāśasyātmano viṣayasaṃvittidvāreṇa grāhakatvamabhivyajyata iti ye
                            vadanti te+api anenaiva nirākṛtāḥ|
                            kecidvimarśātmakatvenātmanaścinmayatvamicchanti| ta āhuḥ --- na
                            vimarśavyatirekeṇa cidrūpatvamātmano nirūpayituṃ śakyam|
                            jaḍādvailakṣaṇyameva cidrūpatvamucyate| tacca vimarśavyatirekeṇa
                            nirūpyamāṇaṃ nānyathā+avatiṣṭhate| --- tadanupapannam| idamitthameva
                            rūpamiti yo vicāraḥ saḥ vimarśa ityucyate| sa cāsmitāvyatirekeṇa
                            notthānameva labhate| tathāhi --- ātmanyupajāyamāno
                            vimarśo+ahamevambhūta ityanenā+a+akāreṇa saṃvedyate|
                            tataścāhaṃśabdasambhinnasyātmalakṣaṇasyārthasya tatra sphuraṇānna tatra
                            vikalpasvarūpatā+atikramaḥ| vikalpaścādhyavasāyātmā buddhidharmo na
                            ciddharmaḥ| kūṭasthanityatvena citeḥ
                            sadaikarūpatvānnityatvānnāhaṅkārānupraveśaḥ| tadanena
                            savimarśatvamātmanaḥ pratipādayatā buddhirevātmatvena bhrāntyā
                            pratipāditā na prakāśātmanaḥ parasya puruṣasya svarūpamavagatamiti|
                            itthaṃ sarveṣveva darśaneṣvadhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ vihāya nānyadātmano
                            rūpamupapadyate| adhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ ca cidrūpatvam| tacca
                            jaḍādvailakṣaṇyameva| cidrūpatayā yadadhitiṣṭhati tadeva bhogyatāṃ
                            nayati| yacca cetanādhiṣṭhitaṃ tadeva sakalavyāpārayogyaṃ bhavati| evaṃ
                            ca sati nityatvāt pradhānasya vyāpāranivṛttau yadātmanaḥ
                            kaivalyamasmābhiruktaṃ tadvihāya darśanāntarāṇāṃ nānyā gatiḥ|
                            tasmādidameva yuktamuktaṃ vṛttisārūpyaparihāreṇa svarūpe pratiṣṭhā
                            citiśakteḥ kaivalyam|
children.translated_text: Not only in our [<s>Sāṃkhya-Yoga</s>] system does the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) in the state of <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) remain of such a nature, namely of the nature of pure consciousness (<s>cit</s>), but even when examined in other philosophical systems, he remains of the same form. For indeed: in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), the Self (<s>ātman</s>) is perceived as consisting of agency, experiencership, and the capacity for reflective awareness. Otherwise, if this single knower of the field were not of such a nature, then—since moments of cognition by themselves, devoid of a continuous reflective subject connecting prior and subsequent [moments], cannot serve as a self—there would be no fixed connection between action and its fruit, and the undesirable consequence of the loss of what was done and the arrival of what was not done [would follow]. If the experiencership belongs to the very same one who performed the action as prescribed by the <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures), then the activity of everyone directed toward attaining what is beneficial and avoiding what is harmful would be possible. Since all practical activity, characterized by acceptance and rejection, is accomplished only through reflective awareness, and since moments of cognition, being mutually distinct, are devoid of such reflective awareness, and since in the absence of that awareness no practical activity whatsoever is possible for anyone—therefore, the one who is the agent, the experiencer, and the reflective subject is established as the Self (<s>ātman</s>). But in the state of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), due to the absence of all practical activity characterized by grasping and the grasped, what remains of him is consciousness alone (<s>caitanya-mātra</s>), and that consciousness is established as mere awareness (<s>citi-mātra</s>), not through self-cognition. For the nature of awareness (<s>citi</s>) is the capacity to grasp objects, not the capacity to grasp itself. For indeed: an object, being grasped by awareness, is cognized as 'this'; but one's own nature, when cognized, [is cognized] as 'I'—and it is not possible to simultaneously perform two operations, outward-directedness and inward-directedness, which are mutually contradictory. Therefore, since it is impossible to perform two operations at one time, [the Self] remains in the form of pure consciousness (<s>cit</s>). Hence, in the state of liberation, when the <s>guṇas</s> have ceased their function, it is proper that the Self remains in the form of mere consciousness alone. But in the state of <s>saṃsāra</s>, agency, experiencership, and reflective awareness all belong to this very same [Self]. For indeed: this beginningless, natural connection with <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial matter), characterized as the relationship of experienced and experiencer, is rooted in non-discriminative cognition (<s>aviveka-khyāti</s>). When this exists, and there is the presence of the two powers constituting the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> (Self), in the conjunction with the transformation into <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) and other evolutes, the Self's sovereignty—its capacity to impart the reflection of consciousness—and the <s>buddhi-sattva</s>'s (intellect's) capacity to receive the transmitted reflection of consciousness, and the determination of agency and experiencership that belongs to <s>buddhi</s> when invested with consciousness—from that alone all practical activity preceded by reflective awareness is accomplished. What need is there for other feeble imaginative speculations? But if, departing from this path, one were to accept the Self's agency and the like as ultimately real, then the undesirable consequence of its being subject to transformation would follow. And from being subject to transformation, due to impermanence, it would not be a Self at all. For just as at one single time, by a single entity of one nature, the experience of mutually contradictory states is not possible—for indeed: in whichever state pleasure has arisen as conjoined with the Self, the experiencership of that belongs to that state, [but] in that very state there is no experiencership of pain. Therefore, from the multiplicity of states, there is multiplicity of the state-possessor that is not different from them. And from multiplicity, due to being subject to transformation, there is no selfhood; nor is there permanence. For this very reason, by the proponents of the quiescent <s>Brahman</s> doctrine, the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, a single nature is accepted for the Self in both the state of <s>saṃsāra</s> and the state of liberation. But those <s>Vedāntins</s> who consider liberation to be the Self's nature of consciousness-and-bliss (<s>cidānandamayatva</s>)—their position is not correct. For indeed: since bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) is of the nature of pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), and since pleasure always appears only as something experienced, and since the status of 'being experienced' is impossible without an act of experiencing that is distinct from it—therefore, from the acceptance of both the experienced and the experiencing, the loss of non-duality [follows]. If, alternatively, one says that its nature is simply pleasure, that is untenable due to the superimposition of contradictory properties. For experiencing and the experienced cannot be one and the same. Moreover, the <s>Advaitins</s> (non-dualists) have accepted the Self as twofold, divided into the individual self (<s>karmātman</s>) and the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>). And in that case, if the supreme Self were to have experiencership of the same form as the individual self's experiencership of pleasure and pain, then the supreme Self would, like the individual self, be subject to transformation and would have ignorance as its nature. But if one says that it does not directly experience, but rather accepts what is presented to it in a detached supervisory capacity—then that is an entry into our [<s>Sāṃkhya-Yoga</s>] position. And the nature of bliss has already been refuted above. Moreover, if [the individual selves] have ignorance as their nature, then since they have no real nature, who would be qualified for scriptural study? Not the supreme Self, since it is eternally liberated and of the nature of knowledge. Nor the individual self, since it has ignorance as its nature. And thus the undesirable consequence of the futility of all scriptures [follows]. And if the world is accepted as consisting of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), one must ask: whose ignorance is it? Not of the supreme Self, since it is eternally liberated and of the nature of knowledge. And if the individual self is, in ultimate reality, without real nature, like a hare's horn—how can there be a connection with ignorance? If it is said: 'This is precisely the nature of ignorance—that it is beyond inquiry'—that which, through inquiry, becomes pure like mist touched by sunlight is called ignorance—this is not correct. For whatever thing produces an effect must necessarily be stated as either different from or identical with something. And the agency of <s>avidyā</s> in producing the effect characterized as <s>saṃsāra</s> must necessarily be accepted. Even granting that, if its indescribability is asserted, then nothing whatsoever could be describable—even <s>Brahman</s> would be subject to the consequence of indescribability. Therefore, no nature other than sovereignty (<s>adhiṣṭhātṛtva</s>) is tenable for the Self. And sovereignty is nothing but the nature of consciousness (<s>cidrūpatva</s>), since there is no valid means of knowledge establishing any other property beyond that. Even those <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others who say that the Self is conscious because of its conjunction with consciousness—even for them, consciousness is born from the conjunction of the Self with <s>manas</s> (mind). For indeed: the qualities such as desire, knowledge, and effort that belong to it arise in the practical state from the conjunction of the Self with <s>manas</s>, and through those very qualities it is designated as knower, agent, and experiencer. But in the state of liberation, upon the cessation of false knowledge, there is also the cessation of the faults rooted in it. The absolute destruction of those specific qualities such as <s>buddhi</s> and the like, [leaving] the Self established in its own nature alone—this is accepted by them. [But] their position is untenable. For in that state, the qualities of permanence, pervasiveness, and the like also belong to space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and such [substances]. Therefore, to distinguish [the Self] from those, the nature of consciousness must necessarily be accepted for the Self. [If one objects:] 'there is connection with the same class (<s>jāti</s>) as non-self'—this is not so, for such class-connection is possible for everything. Therefore, distinction from classes must necessarily be accepted for the Self. Its sovereignty is tenable only as the nature of consciousness, not otherwise. Even those <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> who accept the Self as having the nature of the agent of action—their position too is untenable. For indeed: their thesis is that the Self is grasped in the I-cognition. And in the I-cognition there is both agency and objecthood of the Self itself. But this is untenable due to their mutual contradiction. Agency is the status of being a knower (<s>pramātṛtva</s>); objecthood is the status of being known (<s>prameyatva</s>). And the superimposition of these contradictory properties on a single entity simultaneously is not possible. What has contradictory properties superimposed upon it cannot be one—like existence and non-existence. And agency and objecthood are contradictory. If it is said that the contradiction is not between agency and objecthood but between agency and instrumentality—this is not correct. Since the superimposition of contradictory properties is equal [in both cases], the contradiction is indeed between agency and objecthood, not between agency and objecthood [sic: instrumentality]. Therefore, setting aside the graspability in I-cognition, only the sovereignty of the Self is tenable. And that is nothing but consciousness. Even those who say that the Self's status as grasper is manifested through the medium of object-cognition, claiming that the Self is self-luminous—they too are refuted by this very [argument]. Some desire the consciousness-nature of the Self as consisting of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>). They say: 'The consciousness-nature of the Self cannot be established apart from reflective awareness. What is called consciousness is merely distinction from the insentient. And that, when being determined, does not subsist otherwise than through reflective awareness.'—This is untenable. The inquiry 'this has exactly this nature' is called reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>). And it does not arise at all apart from <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness). For indeed: reflective awareness arising in the Self is experienced in the form 'I am of such a nature.' And therefore, since the meaning characterized as 'self,' combined with the word 'I,' flashes forth there, there is no transcendence of the nature of conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) there. And conceptual construction, being of the nature of determination, is a property of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), not a property of consciousness (<s>cit</s>). Since consciousness, being eternally unchanging (<s>kūṭastha-nitya</s>), is always of one nature, being permanent—there is no entry of ego-sense into it. Therefore, one who establishes the Self as having reflective awareness has, through error, merely established <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) as the Self, and has not comprehended the true nature of the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>, whose nature is pure luminosity (<s>prakāśa</s>). Thus, in all philosophical systems whatsoever, no nature other than sovereignty is tenable for the Self. And sovereignty is the nature of consciousness. And that is merely distinction from the insentient. What is superintended through the nature of consciousness—that alone is led to the status of the experienced. And what is superintended by consciousness alone becomes fit for all activity. This being so, since <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) is permanent, when its activity ceases, the <s>kaivalya</s> of the Self as we have stated—apart from that, other philosophical systems have no other recourse. Therefore, this alone is properly stated: <s>kaivalya</s> is the power of awareness's (<s>citiśakti</s>) establishment in its own nature, through the removal of conformity with the mental modifications (<s>vṛtti-sārūpya</s>).
All kings, whose crowns slip from their bowed heads in service at the feet of his abode of valor, bear his command—
the bearers of the earth [i.e., kings] carry his command upon their bowed heads, their crowns falling in obeisance at his feet;
the goddess of speech, having reached his lotus-face, has taken refuge with incomparable pride—
that <s>Śrī Bhojapati</s> (Lord <s>Bhoja</s>) composed a commentary on the <s>sūtras</s> made by the Lord of Hooded Serpents (<s>Patañjali</s>).

children.text:
iti śrīdhāreśvarabhojadevaviracitāyāṃ rājamārtaṇḍābhidhāyāṃ
                        pātañjalavṛttau kaivalyapādaścaturthaḥ | samāptaścāyaṃ granthaḥ | ||om
                        śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Rājamārtaṇḍa</s>, the commentary on <s>Patañjali</s>'s [<s>Yoga Sūtras</s>] composed by <s>Bhojadeva</s>, Lord of <s>Dhārā</s>, this is the fourth chapter, the <s>Kaivalya Pāda</s> (Chapter on Liberation). And this work is completed. || <s>Oṃ</s> peace, peace, peace ||
Now, the <s>Yoga Sūtras</s> of <s>Patañjali</s>.
Now, the <s>Samādhi Pāda</s> (Chapter on Concentration). ||1||
Now, the teaching of <s>Yoga</s>. ||Samādhi 1||
<s>Yoga</s> is the cessation of the modifications of the mind. ||Samādhi 2||
Then the seer abides in its own nature. ||Samādhi 3|| At other times, [there is] identification with the modifications. ||Samādhi 4||

children.text:
vṛttayaḥ pañcatayyaḥ kliṣṭākliṣṭāḥ ||samādhi 5||
                        pramāṇaviparyayavikalpanidrāsmṛtayaḥ ||samādhi 6|| pratyakṣānumānāgamāḥ
                        pramāṇāni ||samādhi 7||
children.translated_text: The modifications are fivefold, afflicted and non-afflicted. ||Samādhi 5|| [They are] valid cognition, error, conceptualization, sleep, and memory. ||Samādhi 6|| Perception, inference, and verbal testimony are the valid means of knowledge. ||Samādhi 7||

children.text:
viparyayo mithyājñānamatadrūpapratiṣṭham ||samādhi 8|| śabdajñānānupātī
                        vastuśūnyo vikalpaḥ ||samādhi 9|| abhāvapratyayālambanā vṛttirnidrā
                        ||samādhi 10|| anubhūtaviṣayāsampramoṣaḥ smṛtiḥ ||samādhi 11||
                        abhyāsavairāgyābhyāṃ tannirodhaḥ ||samādhi 12||
children.translated_text: Error is false knowledge not established in the true form [of the object]. ||Samādhi 8|| <s>Vikalpa</s> (conceptualization) follows verbal knowledge and is devoid of a corresponding object. ||Samādhi 9|| Sleep is that modification which has the cognition of absence as its support. ||Samādhi 10|| Memory is the non-deprivation of an experienced object. ||Samādhi 11|| Their cessation is achieved through practice and detachment. ||Samādhi 12||
Therein, the effort toward steadiness is <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice). ||Samādhi 13||
But that becomes firmly grounded when practiced for a long time, without interruption, and with devotion. ||Samādhi 14||
The consciousness of mastery in one who is free from craving for objects seen or heard about is <s>vairāgya</s> (detachment). ||Samādhi 15||

The supreme [<s>vairāgya</s>] is freedom from craving for the <s>guṇas</s>, arising from the discernment of <s>Puruṣa</s>. ||Samādhi 16|| <s>Samprajñāta</s> [<s>samādhi</s>] is accompanied by deliberation, reflection, bliss, and I-am-ness. ||Samādhi 17||
The other [<s>samādhi</s>] is preceded by the practice of the cause of cessation, and only latent impressions remain. ||Samādhi 18||

For the bodiless ones and those merged in <s>Prakṛti</s>, [<s>samādhi</s>] is caused by continued existence. ||Samādhi 19|| For the others, it is preceded by faith, energy, mindfulness, <s>samādhi</s>, and wisdom. ||Samādhi 20||

children.text:
tīvrasaṃvegānāmāsannaḥ ||samādhi 21|| mṛdumadhyādhimātratvāttato+api viśeṣaḥ
                        ||samādhi 22|| īśvarapraṇidhānādvā ||samādhi 23||
                        kleśakarmavipākāśayairaparāmṛṣṭaḥ puruṣaviśeṣa īśvaraḥ ||samādhi 24||
children.translated_text: For those with intense ardor, [<s>samādhi</s>] is near. ||Samādhi 21|| There is further distinction due to mild, moderate, and intense degrees. ||Samādhi 22|| Or by devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). ||Samādhi 23|| <s>Īśvara</s> is a special <s>Puruṣa</s>, untouched by afflictions, actions, their results, and latent deposits. ||Samādhi 24||
In Him, the seed of omniscience is unsurpassed. ||Samādhi 25||

children.text:
sa pūrveṣāmapi guruḥ kālenānavacchedāt ||samādhi 26|| tasya vācakaḥ praṇavaḥ
                        ||samādhi 27|| tajjapastadarthabhāvanam ||samādhi 28||
children.translated_text: He is the teacher even of the ancients, because He is not limited by time. ||Samādhi 26|| His designator is <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>). ||Samādhi 27|| Its repetition and meditation on its meaning [should be practiced]. ||Samādhi 28||

From that comes the attainment of inward-directed consciousness and also the absence of obstacles. ||Samādhi 29|| Disease, dullness, doubt, negligence, laziness, non-abstention, erroneous perception, failure to attain a stage, and instability—these are the distractions of the mind, and they are the obstacles. ||Samādhi 30|| Suffering, depression, trembling of the body, and disturbed inhalation and exhalation are the companions of distraction. ||Samādhi 31||
For their prevention, the practice of one principle [should be performed]. ||Samādhi 32||
By cultivating friendliness, compassion, joy, and equanimity toward the happy, the suffering, the virtuous, and the non-virtuous [respectively], the mind becomes serene. ||Samādhi 33||
Or by the expulsion and retention of <s>prāṇa</s> (breath). ||Samādhi 34||
Or the arising of object-directed activity, which binds the mind to steadiness. ||Samādhi 35||
Or [activity that is] sorrowless and luminous. ||Samādhi 36||

children.text:
vītarāgaviṣayaṃ vā cittam ||samādhi 37|| svapnanidrājñānālambanaṃ vā
                        ||samādhi 38|| yathābhimatadhyānādvā ||samādhi 39||
                        paramāṇuparamamahattvānto+asya vaśīkāraḥ ||samādhi 40||
                        kṣīṇavṛtterabhijātasyeva maṇergrahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyeṣu tatsthatadañjanatā
                        samāpattiḥ ||samādhi 41|| śabdārthajñānavikalpaiḥ saṅkīrṇā savitarkā
                        samāpattiḥ ||samādhi 42||
children.translated_text: Or a mind [directed toward] one who is free from attachment. ||Samādhi 37|| Or [having] dream or sleep experience as support. ||Samādhi 38|| Or by meditation on whatever is agreeable. ||Samādhi 39|| His mastery extends from the smallest atom to the greatest magnitude. ||Samādhi 40|| For one whose modifications have weakened, like a flawless crystal, <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) is the taking on of the color of the grasper, grasping, or grasped, upon which [the mind] rests and by which it is tinged. ||Samādhi 41|| <s>Savitarka samāpatti</s> is that which is mixed with conceptual alternatives of word, meaning, and knowledge. ||Samādhi 42||

children.text:
smṛtipariśuddhau svarūpaśūnyevā+arthamātranirbhāsā nirvitarkā ||samādhi 43||
                        etayaiva savicārā nirvicārā ca sūkṣmaviṣayā vyākhyātā ||samadhi 44||
children.translated_text: When memory is purified, as if empty of its own nature, shining forth as the object alone—that is <s>nirvitarka</s> [samāpatti]. ||Samādhi 43|| By this very [explanation], <s>savicāra</s> and <s>nirvicāra</s> [samāpattis], which have subtle objects, are explained. ||Samādhi 44||
And the subtlety of objects extends up to the unmanifest (<s>aliṅga</s>). ||Samādhi 45||
Those very [samāpattis] constitute <s>sabīja samādhi</s> (samādhi with seed). ||Samādhi 46|| When there is clarity in <s>nirvicāra</s>, there is inner luminosity. ||Samādhi 47||
Therein, the wisdom is truth-bearing (<s>ṛtambharā</s>). ||Samādhi 48||
This wisdom has a different domain from that born of scripture and inference, since it pertains to particulars. ||Samādhi 49||
The latent impression born of that obstructs other latent impressions. ||Samādhi 50||
When even that is ceased, from the cessation of all, seedless (<s>nirbīja</s>) <s>samādhi</s> [arises]. ||Samādhi 51||
Thus ends the <s>Samādhi Pāda</s>. ||1||
Now, the <s>Sādhana Pāda</s> (Chapter on Practice). ||2||

children.text:
tapaḥ svādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni kriyāyogaḥ ||sādhana 1|| samādhibhāvanārthaḥ
                        kleśatanūkaraṇārthaśca ||sādhana 2|| avidyā+asmitārāgadveṣābhiniveśāḥ kleśāḥ
                        ||sādhana 3||
children.translated_text: <s>Tapas</s> (austerity), <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), and <s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s> (devotion to the Lord) constitute <s>Kriyāyoga</s>. ||Sādhana 1|| [It is] for the purpose of cultivating <s>samādhi</s> and for attenuating the afflictions. ||Sādhana 2|| Ignorance, I-am-ness, attachment, aversion, and clinging to life are the afflictions. ||Sādhana 3||

Ignorance is the field for the others, whether dormant, attenuated, alternating, or fully active. ||Sādhana 4|| Ignorance is seeing the eternal, pure, pleasurable, and the Self in what is non-eternal, impure, painful, and not-Self. ||Sādhana 5||
I-am-ness is the seeming identity of the powers of seeing and of the instrument of seeing. ||Sādhana 6|| Attachment follows upon pleasure. ||Sādhana 7||
Aversion follows upon pain. ||Sādhana 8||
Clinging to life flows on by its own momentum and is established even in the wise. ||Sādhana 9||
These, in their subtle form, are to be overcome by inverse propagation. ||Sādhana 10|| Their modifications are to be overcome by meditation. ||Sādhana 11||
The repository of actions, rooted in afflictions, is experienced in the seen and unseen births. ||Sādhana 12||
As long as the root exists, its ripening [manifests as] birth, lifespan, and experience. ||Sādhana 13||

children.text:
te hlādaparitāpaphalāḥ puṇyāpuṇyahetutvāt ||sādhana 14||
                        pariṇāmatāpasaṃskāraduḥkhairguṇavṛttivirodhācca duḥkhameva sarvaṃ vivekinaḥ
                        ||sādhana 15||
children.translated_text: These have pleasure and pain as their fruits, caused by virtue and vice. ||Sādhana 14|| Due to the sufferings of transformation, anxiety, and latent impressions, and due to the conflict of the activities of the <s>guṇas</s>, for the discerning person, all is suffering. ||Sādhana 15||
The suffering that has not yet come is to be avoided. ||Sādhana 16||
The conjunction of the seer and the seen is the cause of that which is to be avoided. ||Sādhana 17||

children.text:
prakāśakriyāsthitiśīlaṃ bhūtendriyātmakaṃ bhogāpavargārthaṃ dṛśyam ||sādhana
                        18|| viśeṣāviśeṣaliṅgamātrāliṅgāni guṇaparvāṇi ||sādhana 19|| draṣṭā
                        dṛśimātraḥ śuddho+api pratyayānupaśyaḥ ||sādhana 20|| tadartha eva
                        dṛśyasyātmā ||sādhana 21||
children.translated_text: The seen has the nature of illumination, activity, and stability, consists of elements and senses, and has the purpose of experience and liberation. ||Sādhana 18|| The particular, the non-particular, the merely indicated, and the unmanifest are the stages of the <s>guṇas</s>. ||Sādhana 19|| The seer is mere seeing, though pure, perceives through the intellect. ||Sādhana 20|| The very existence of the seen is for the sake of the seer. ||Sādhana 21||
Though destroyed for one whose purpose is fulfilled, [the seen] is not destroyed, being common to others. ||Sādhana 22||
The conjunction [of seer and seen] is the cause of the apprehension of the essential nature of the owned and the owner. ||Sādhana 23||
Its cause is ignorance. ||Sādhana 24||

children.text:
tadabhāve saṃyogābhāvo hānaṃ taddṛśeḥ kaivalyam ||sādhana 25||
                        vivekakhyātiraviplavā hānopāyaḥ ||sādhana 26||
children.translated_text: In its absence, the conjunction disappears—that is the abandonment; that is <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) of the seer. ||Sādhana 25|| Unwavering discriminative discernment is the means of abandonment. ||Sādhana 26||
His wisdom at the final stage is sevenfold. ||Sādhana 27||

children.text: tasya saptadhā prāntabhūmiḥ prajñā iti vā bahusammataḥ sūtrapāṭhaḥ

children.translated_text: From the practice of the limbs of <s>yoga</s>, upon the destruction of impurity, the light of knowledge [shines forth] up to discriminative discernment. ||Sādhana 28|| <s>Yama</s> (restraints), <s>niyama</s> (observances), <s>āsana</s> (posture), <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal), <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) are the eight limbs. ||Sādhana 29||
Non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possessiveness are the <s>yamas</s> (restraints). ||Sādhana 30||

When not limited by class, place, time, or occasion, [the yamas] are universal and constitute the great vow. ||Sādhana 31|| Purity, contentment, austerity, self-study, and devotion to the Lord are the <s>niyamas</s> (observances). ||Sādhana 32||
When disturbed by negative thoughts, [one should practice] cultivation of the opposite. ||Sādhana 33||

children.text:
vitarkā hiṃsādayaḥ kṛtakāritānumoditā lobhakrodhamohapūrvakā
                        mṛdumadhyādhimātrā duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāavanam ||sādhana
                        34|| ahiṃsāpratiṣṭhāyāṃ tatsannidhau vairatyāgaḥ ||sādhana 35||
                        satyapratiṣṭhāyāṃ kriyāphalāśrayatvam ||sādhana 36|| asteyapratiṣṭhāyāṃ
                        sarvaratnopasthānam ||sādhana 37|| brahmacaryapratiṣṭhāyāṃ vīryalābhaḥ
                        ||sādhana 38|| aparigrahasthairye janmakathantāsambodhaḥ ||sādhana 39||
                        śaucātsvāṅgajugupsā parairasaṃsargaḥ ||sādhana 40||
                        sattvaśuddhisaumanasyaikāgratendriyajayātmadarśanayogyatvāni ca ||sādhana
                        41||
children.translated_text: Negative thoughts such as violence—whether done, caused to be done, or approved; whether preceded by greed, anger, or delusion; whether mild, moderate, or intense—result in endless suffering and ignorance. Such is the cultivation of the opposite. ||Sādhana 34|| When non-violence is firmly established, hostility is abandoned in one's presence. ||Sādhana 35|| When truthfulness is established, actions and their fruits become dependent [on one's word]. ||Sādhana 36|| When non-stealing is established, all gems present themselves. ||Sādhana 37|| When celibacy is established, vigor is obtained. ||Sādhana 38|| When non-possessiveness is firm, knowledge of the 'how' of births [arises]. ||Sādhana 39|| From purity, disgust toward one's own body and non-contact with others. ||Sādhana 40|| And purity of <s>sattva</s>, cheerfulness, one-pointedness, mastery of the senses, and fitness for the vision of the Self. ||Sādhana 41||
From contentment, unsurpassed happiness is obtained. ||Sādhana 42||

Perfection of the body and senses from austerity, through the destruction of impurity. ||Sādhana 43|| From self-study, union with the desired deity. ||Sādhana 44|| Perfection of <s>samādhi</s> from devotion to the Lord. ||Sādhana 45|| Posture is steady and comfortable. ||Sādhana 46|| By relaxation of effort and absorption on the infinite. ||Sādhana 47||
From that, non-affliction by the pairs of opposites. ||Sādhana 48||
When that is mastered, <s>prāṇāyāma</s> is the cutting off of the movement of inhalation and exhalation. ||Sādhana 49||
It has external, internal, and suspension operations, regulated by place, time, and number, becoming long and subtle. ||Sādhana 50||
The fourth [<s>prāṇāyāma</s>] transcends the domain of external and internal. ||Sādhana 51||
From that, the covering of light is diminished. ||Sādhana 52||

children.text:
dhāraṇāsu ca yogyatā manasaḥ ||sādhana 53|| svaviṣayāsamprayoge
                        cittasvarūpānukāra ivendriyāṇāṃ pratyāhāraḥ ||sādhana 54||
children.translated_text: And fitness of the mind for concentrations. ||Sādhana 53|| <s>Pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal) is as it were the imitation by the senses of the mind's own nature, when disjoined from their objects. ||Sādhana 54||
From that, supreme mastery of the senses. ||Sādhana 55||
Thus ends the <s>Sādhana Pāda</s>. ||2||
Now, the <s>Vibhūti Pāda</s> (Chapter on Powers). ||3||
<s>Dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) is the binding of the mind to a place. ||Vibhūti 1||

children.text:
tatra pratyayaikatānatā dhyānam ||vibhūti 2|| tadevārthamātranirbhāsaṃ
                        svarūpaśūnyamiva samādhiḥ ||vibhūti 3||
children.translated_text: Therein, the continuous flow of cognition toward [the object] is <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). ||Vibhūti 2|| That very [meditation], when shining forth as the object alone, as if empty of its own form, is <s>samādhi</s>. ||Vibhūti 3||
The three together constitute <s>saṃyama</s>. ||Vibhūti 4||
From mastery of that, the light of wisdom [arises]. ||Vibhūti 5||
Its application is to the stages [of practice]. ||Vibhūti 6|| The three [inner limbs] are more internal than the preceding [five]. ||Vibhūti 7||

Even that is external to the seedless [<s>samādhi</s>]. ||Vibhūti 8|| The <s>nirodha-pariṇāma</s> (transformation of cessation) is the connection of the mind with the moment of cessation, when the emerging and subsiding latent impressions of emergence and cessation [alternate]. ||Vibhūti 9||

children.text:
tasya praśāntavāhitā saṃskārāt ||vibhūti 10|| sarvārthataikāgratayoḥ
                        kṣayodayau cittasya samādhipariṇāmaḥ ||vibhūti 11||
children.translated_text: Its peaceful flow [comes] from latent impression. ||Vibhūti 10|| The <s>samādhi-pariṇāma</s> (transformation of concentration) is the decline of all-objectness and the rise of one-pointedness in the mind. ||Vibhūti 11||
The <s>ekāgratā-pariṇāma</s> (transformation of one-pointedness) is when the subsiding and arising cognitions are similar in the mind. ||Vibhūti 12||

children.text:
etena bhūtendriyeṣu dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmā vyākhyātāḥ ||vibhūti 13||
                        śāntoditāvyapadeśyadharmānupātī dharmī ||vibhūti 14|| kramānyatvaṃ
                        pariṇāmānyatve hetuḥ ||vibhūti 15|| pariṇāmatrayasaṃyamādatītānāgatajñānam
                        ||vibhūti 16||
                        śabdārthapratyayānāmitaretarādhyāsātsaṅkarastatpravibhāgasaṃyamātsarvabh
                        ūtarutajñānam ||vibhūti 17|| saṃskārasākṣātkaraṇātpūrvajātijñānam ||vibhūti
                        18|| pratyayasya paracittajñānam ||vibhūti 19||
children.translated_text: By this, the transformations of <s>dharma</s> (property), <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (temporal character), and <s>avasthā</s> (condition) in the elements and sense organs are explained. ||Vibhūti 13|| The <s>dharmin</s> (substance) is that which follows the subsided, arisen, and indeterminate <s>dharmas</s> (properties). ||Vibhūti 14|| The difference in sequence is the cause of the difference in transformation. ||Vibhūti 15|| By <s>saṃyama</s> on the three transformations, knowledge of the past and future [arises]. ||Vibhūti 16|| Due to the mutual superimposition of word, meaning, and cognition, there is confusion; by <s>saṃyama</s> on their distinction, knowledge of the sounds of all beings [arises]. ||Vibhūti 17|| By direct perception of <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions), knowledge of previous births [arises]. ||Vibhūti 18|| Knowledge of another's mind [arises from <s>saṃyama</s>] on the mental content. ||Vibhūti 19||

children.text:
na ca tatsālambanaṃ tasyāviṣayībhūtatvāt ||vibhūti 20||
                        kāyarūpasaṃyamāttadgrāhyaśaktistambhe cakṣuṣprakāśāsaṃyoge+antardhānam
                        ||vibhūti 21||
children.translated_text: But that [knowledge] is not together with its support, because [the support] has not become the object [of <s>saṃyama</s>]. ||Vibhūti 20|| By <s>saṃyama</s> on the form of the body, upon the suspension of the power of being perceived, when the connection between the eye and light is severed—invisibility [results]. ||Vibhūti 21||

children.text:
sopakramaṃ nirupakramaṃ ca karma tatsaṃyamādaparāntajñānamariṣṭebhyo vā
                        ||vibhūti 22||
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> is of two kinds: with active fruition (<s>sopakrama</s>) and with deferred fruition (<s>nirupakrama</s>); by <s>saṃyama</s> on that, or from omens, knowledge of death [arises]. ||Vibhūti 22||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>) and the like, strengths [arise]. ||Vibhūti 23||

[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on strengths, the strength of an elephant and the like [arise]. ||Vibhūti 24|| By directing the light of higher perception (<s>pravṛttyāloka</s>), knowledge of the subtle, the concealed, and the distant [arises]. ||Vibhūti 25||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the sun, knowledge of the worlds [arises]. ||Vibhūti 26||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the moon, knowledge of the arrangement of the stars [arises]. ||Vibhūti 27||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the pole star (<s>Dhruva</s>), knowledge of their movements [arises]. ||Vibhūti 28||

[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the navel center (<s>nābhicakra</s>), knowledge of the arrangement of the body [arises]. ||Vibhūti 29|| [By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the throat pit (<s>kaṇṭhakūpa</s>), cessation of hunger and thirst [results]. ||Vibhūti 30||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the <s>kūrma nāḍī</s> (tortoise channel), steadiness [results]. ||Vibhūti 31||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the light at the crown of the head (<s>mūrdhajyotis</s>), vision of the <s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings) [results]. ||Vibhūti 32||
Or, from <s>prātibha</s> (intuitive illumination), [knowledge of] everything [arises]. ||Vibhūti 33||
[By <s>saṃyama</s>] on the heart, knowledge of the mind [arises]. ||Vibhūti 34||

Experience (<s>bhoga</s>) is the non-distinction in cognition between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, which are utterly unmixed; by <s>saṃyama</s> on the purpose-for-itself as distinct from the purpose-for-another, knowledge of <s>Puruṣa</s> [arises]. ||Vibhūti 35||

children.text:
tataḥ prātibhaśrāvaṇavedanādarśāsvādavārtā jāyante ||vibhūti 36|| te
                        samādhāvupasargā vyutthāne siddhayaḥ ||vibhūti 37||
                        bandhakāraṇaśaithilyātpracārasaṃvedanācca cittasya paraśarīrāveśaḥ ||vibhūti
                        38|| udānajayājjalapaṅkakaṇṭakādiṣvasaṅga utkrāntiśca ||vibhūti 39||
children.translated_text: From that, <s>prātibha</s> (intuitive), <s>śrāvaṇa</s> (auditory), <s>vedanā</s> (tactile), <s>ādarśa</s> (visual), <s>āsvāda</s> (gustatory), and <s>vārtā</s> (olfactory) [perceptions] arise. ||Vibhūti 36|| These are obstacles to <s>samādhi</s>, [but] in the outward-directed state (<s>vyutthāna</s>), they are <s>siddhis</s> (powers). ||Vibhūti 37|| By the loosening of the cause of bondage and by the knowledge of the mind's channels of movement, entry into another's body [is achieved]. ||Vibhūti 38|| By mastery of <s>udāna</s>, non-contact with water, mud, thorns, and the like, and ascension [at death result]. ||Vibhūti 39||
By mastery of <s>samāna</s>, radiance [results]. ||Vibhūti 40||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the relation between the ear and space, divine hearing [arises]. ||Vibhūti 41||
By <s>saṃyama</s> on the relation between the body and space, and by <s>samāpatti</s> (absorption) on the lightness of cotton, traversing space [is achieved]. ||Vibhūti 42||

The external, non-imagined modification is the <s>mahāvidehā</s> (great disembodied state); from that, the destruction of the covering of light [results]. ||Vibhūti 43|| By <s>saṃyama</s> on the gross, own-nature, subtle, inherent relation, and purposefulness [of the elements], mastery over the elements [is achieved]. ||Vibhūti 44||

From that arise <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and the other [powers], perfection of the body, and non-obstruction by the properties [of the elements]. ||Vibhūti 45|| Perfection of the body (<s>kāyasampat</s>) is beauty of form, grace, strength, and diamond-like hardness. ||Vibhūti 46|| By <s>saṃyama</s> on the grasping, own-nature, <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness), inherent relation, and purposefulness [of the senses], mastery over the senses [is achieved]. ||Vibhūti 47||

children.text:
tato manojavitvaṃ vikaraṇabhāvaḥ pradhānajayaśca ||vibhūti 48||
                        sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrasya sarvabhāvādhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ sarvajñātṛtvaṃ ca
                        ||vibhūti 49||
children.translated_text: From that [arise] speed of the mind, the state of being without instruments (<s>vikaraṇabhāva</s>), and mastery over <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial nature). ||Vibhūti 48|| For one who has only the discernment of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, sovereignty over all states of being and omniscience [result]. ||Vibhūti 49||
From dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) even toward that, upon the destruction of the seed of defects, <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) [arises]. ||Vibhūti 50||

children.text:
svāmyupanimantraṇe saṅgasmayā+akaraṇaṃ punaraniṣṭaprasaṅgāt ||vibhūti 51||
                        kṣaṇatatkramayoḥ saṃyamādvivekajaṃ jñānam ||vibhūti 52||
                        jātilakṣaṇadeśairanyatānavacchedāttulyayostataḥ pratipattiḥ ||vibhūti
                        53||
children.translated_text: Upon the invitation of those in high places, [one should practice] non-attachment and non-pride, because of the possibility of the recurrence of the undesirable. ||Vibhūti 51|| By <s>saṃyama</s> on the moment and its succession, knowledge born of discrimination [arises]. ||Vibhūti 52|| Therefrom [arises] discernment of two things that are alike, when the distinction by class, characteristic, and position is not the [basis of] differentiation. ||Vibhūti 53||

children.text:
tārakaṃ sarvaviṣayaṃ sarvathāviṣayamakramaṃ ceti vivekajaṃ jñānam ||vibhūti
                        54||
children.translated_text: The knowledge born of discrimination is <s>tāraka</s> (liberating), has all objects [as its scope], has all conditions [as its scope], and is non-sequential. ||Vibhūti 54||
When there is equality of purity between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, [there is] <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). ||Vibhūti 55||
Thus ends the <s>Vibhūti Pāda</s> (Chapter on Supernatural Powers). ||3||
Now the <s>Kaivalya Pāda</s> (Chapter on Liberation). ||4||
The <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers) arise from birth, herbs, <s>mantras</s>, <s>tapas</s> (austerity), and <s>samādhi</s>. ||Kaivalya 1||
The transformation into another birth [is effected] by the overflow of <s>prakṛti</s> (nature). ||Kaivalya 2||
The instrumental cause does not set the <s>prakṛtis</s> (natural tendencies) in motion; but from it comes the breaking of the barrier—like a farmer. ||Kaivalya 3||
The created minds [arise] from <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness) alone. ||Kaivalya 4||
Though their activities differ, the one mind is the impeller of the many. ||Kaivalya 5||

children.text:
tatra dhyānajamanāśayam ||kaivalya 6|| karmāśuklākṛṣṇaṃ
                        yoginastrividhamitareṣām ||kaivalya 7||
                        tatastadvipākānuguṇānāmevābhivyaktirvāsanānām ||kaivalya 8||
                        jātideśakālavyavahitānāmapyānantaryaṃ smṛtisaṃskārayorekarūpatvāt ||kaivalya
                        9||
children.translated_text: Among these, the <s>dhyāna</s>-born (meditation-born) mind is free from residual impressions (<s>anāśaya</s>). ||Kaivalya 6|| The <s>karma</s> of a yogin is neither white nor black; for others, it is threefold. ||Kaivalya 7|| From that, the manifestation of only those <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) that correspond to the fruition [of that <s>karma</s>]. ||Kaivalya 8|| Even though separated by birth, place, and time, there is continuity [of <s>vāsanās</s>], because memory and <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions) are of one form. ||Kaivalya 9||
And those [<s>vāsanās</s>] are beginningless, because the will to live (<s>āśis</s>) is eternal. ||Kaivalya 10||

Since they are held together by cause, fruit, support, and object—in the absence of these, their absence [follows]. ||Kaivalya 11|| The past and the future exist in their own form, due to the difference of time-paths of the <s>dharmas</s> (properties). ||Kaivalya 12||

They are manifest and subtle, having the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents of nature) as their nature. ||Kaivalya 13|| The reality of the object [is established] because of the unity of transformation. ||Kaivalya 14||

children.text:
vastusāmye cittabhedāttayorviviktaḥ panthāḥ ||kaivalya 15||
                        taduparāgāpekṣitvāccittasya vastu jñātājñātam ||kaivalya 16||
children.translated_text: The object being the same, due to the difference of minds, the paths of the two are distinct. ||Kaivalya 15|| An object is known or unknown to the mind, depending on the mind's coloring by it. ||Kaivalya 16||
The modifications of the mind are always known, because of the unchangingness of their lord, <s>Puruṣa</s>. ||Kaivalya 17||
It [the mind] is not self-illuminating, because it is an object of perception (<s>dṛśya</s>). ||Kaivalya 18||
And at one time, there is no ascertainment of both [subject and object simultaneously]. ||Kaivalya 19||

If the mind were perceived by another mind, there would be an infinite regress of cognitions of cognitions, and confusion of memory. ||Kaivalya 20|| When consciousness (<s>citi</s>), which does not pass over [to another form], assumes the form of that [mind], self-cognition [results]. ||Kaivalya 21||
The mind, colored by both the seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>) and the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>), [comprehends] all objects. ||Kaivalya 22||
Though variegated by innumerable <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions), [the mind] exists for the sake of another (<s>parārtha</s>), because it acts in combination. ||Kaivalya 23||
For one who sees the distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>), the cultivation of the sense of selfhood (<s>ātmabhāvabhāvanā</s>) ceases. ||Kaivalya 24||
Then the mind, inclined toward discrimination (<s>vivekanimna</s>), gravitates toward <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). ||Kaivalya 25||
In the gaps of that [discriminative knowledge], other mental contents arise from <s>saṃskāras</s> (latent impressions). ||Kaivalya 26||
The removal of these has been stated [to be] like [the removal of] the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). ||Kaivalya 27||

children.text:
prasaṅkhyāne+apyakusīdasya sarvathā vivekakhyāterdharmameghaḥ samādhiḥ
                        ||kaivalya 28|| tataḥ kleśakarmanivṛttiḥ ||kaivalya 29||
children.translated_text: For one who is not interested even in the highest meditation (<s>prasaṅkhyāna</s>), from discriminative discernment (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) in every way, [there arises] <s>dharma-megha samādhi</s> (the cloud-of-dharma absorption). ||Kaivalya 28|| From that, the cessation of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>karma</s> [results]. ||Kaivalya 29||
Then, because of the infinity of knowledge freed from all obscuring impurities, what remains to be known is little. ||Kaivalya 30||
From that, the cessation of the sequence of transformations of the <s>guṇas</s>, whose purpose has been fulfilled. ||Kaivalya 31||
Sequence (<s>krama</s>) is the correlative of the moment, apprehensible at the final end of transformation. ||Kaivalya 32||

children.text:
puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ guṇānāṃ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṃ svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā
                        citiśakteriti ||kaivalya 33||
children.translated_text: The re-absorption (<s>pratiprasava</s>) of the <s>guṇas</s>, devoid of purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s>, is <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation)—or [it is] the establishment of the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>) in its own nature. ||Kaivalya 33||
Thus ends the <s>Kaivalya Pāda</s> (Chapter on Liberation). ||4||
Thus [end] the <s>Pātañjala Yogasūtras</s>.
